stem:
Leela asks whether $\dfrac{7}{20}$ can be written as a terminating decimal by finding an equivalent fraction with denominator $10$, $100$, $1000$, and so on.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $\dfrac{7}{20}$ cannot become a terminating decimal, even though an equivalent fraction $\dfrac{35}{100}$ exists.
Writing the terminating decimal $0.35$ is what creates the equivalent fraction $\dfrac{35}{100}$.
Rewrite $\dfrac{7}{20}$ as a continuing never-ending decimal only, and stop.

teacher.key_rationale: Multiply numerator and denominator by 5 to reach 35/100 = 0.35. Denying the equivalent fraction, reversing decimal-creates-fraction, or forcing a never-ending form all miss that conversion.
